# Omni View Europe
> **Three hundred sixty billion euros in China deficit opens two days of Brussels talks short of a budget deal.**

**What You Need to Know:** A China trade deficit of three hundred sixty billion euros is on the table as European Union leaders open two days of talks in Brussels that are not expected to settle the next long-term budget. Energy prices and Friday's session on Ukraine sit beside that argument. Elsewhere, student protests in Tirana turned violent, and a Guardian series measures how far Polish incomes have climbed since the Soviet era.

### Lead
**EU summit to focus on China, Ukraine and bloc budget: DW**
European Union leaders opened talks in Brussels on Thursday on competition from China, energy prices and the bloc budget for 2028 to 2034, with support for Ukraine due on Friday and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy invited. DW reports the deficit with China reached €360 billion ($400.4 billion) last year and is set to exceed that this year; the European Commission agreed with Beijing last week to curb hybrid-car imports, and trade chief Maroš Šefčovič's preliminary deal also covers access to rare earths. The EU accuses China of unfair state subsidies, industry groups say the import surge is closing factories, and Chancellor Friedrich Merz and President Emmanuel Macron want measures against market distortion, including a Franco-German "kill switch" that would cut China's market access if the deficit stayed unsustainable. Euronews reports oil remains above $100 a barrel despite a coordinated G7 release, and the International Energy Agency warned on Wednesday of renewed wholesale diesel price rises in Europe; Italian and Greek leaders want fiscal rules eased for temporary price measures, while more fiscally conservative states warn that would add to deficits and volatility. The seven-year budget needs unanimous approval; European Council President António Costa wants a deal by the end of the year so the law can be finished before January 2028, an Irish compromise has left both frugal governments and supporters of a larger budget unhappy, and a senior diplomat said leaders are not in a hurry and want a good deal rather than a fast one. DW says this summit is not expected to produce a breakthrough, a special summit is set for November, and pressure is rising ahead of elections next year in several member states; Euronews adds that Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's call for snap elections in Spain adds uncertainty. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told Euronews the US-Russia diesel deal is a "gift to Putin," that "the majority of the financing of this war comes from oil," and that strikes on Russian refineries fit "defence of Ukraine" under international law. Zelenskyy told Piers Morgan he feels "betrayed" and that Ukraine is losing American support "not because of us"; Euronews, citing the Financial Times, reports US negotiators proposed that European countries unfreeze some immobilised Russian state assets into a vehicle controlled by Washington, a plan European delegates rejected in Miami last week, with a loan to Ukraine due to be raised in Brussels on Friday. Source: [dw.com](https://www.dw.com/en/eu-summit-to-focus-on-china-ukraine-and-bloc-budget/a-79665338?maca=en-rss-en-eu-2092-rdf) Source: [euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/15/eu-leaders-enter-crunch-talks-on-energy-china-and-the-budget) Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261015-eu-leaders-head-for-showdown-over-bloc-budget)

### Across the Region
**Student protests in Albania turn violent as demonstrators clash with police: The Guardian**
Tens of thousands of students marched in Tirana over education costs and corruption, the Guardian reports, setting a government building and two banks alight and throwing stones at police. Officers used water cannon and tear gas; a fire started at the education ministry, a nearby branch of Raiffeisen Bank caught fire, bins were overturned, shopfronts were smashed, and dozens of people were detained. France 24 reports the protests turned violent for a second night on Wednesday, with several government buildings damaged and at least one ablaze. Thousands demanded that Prime Minister Edi Rama resign and that university conditions improve. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/14/student-protests-tirana-albania-police-clashes) Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261014-albania-protests-protestors-demand-pm-rama-resignation)

**French anti-terror investigators probe True Crime Community link to school shooting: France 24**
The French anti-terrorism prosecutor has taken over the investigation into a school shooting near Marseille. An initial probe found the 14-year-old suspect appeared to belong to a group called the True Crime Community. A student opened fire with a hunting rifle that had been hidden inside a guitar case, and two teachers were shot and wounded. Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/a-propos/20261014-french-anti-terror-investigators-probe-true-crime-community-link-to-school-shooting)

**Rising Violence is a Sign that Serbia’s Ruling Party is Panicking: Balkan Insight**
Balkan Insight reports a run of street incidents in the weeks before Serbia's parliamentary elections on October 25, and links them to nervousness in the ruling Serbian Progressive Party about the vote. In Užice, the paper says party supporters beat citizens during a protest against a visit by Aleksandar Vučić while police stood by; in Belgrade, men attacked and injured an observer from the Anti-Corruption Agency at a ruling-party stand. In Novi Sad, supporters led by a party candidate confronted the opposition student-led list and tried to seize a banner. Mayor Aleksandar Šapić was reported to have assaulted a female opposition councillor; he denied it. An N1 journalist was attacked in Belgrade, a journalist in Niš was injured while filming a party event with police reportedly refusing to step in, and Momčilo Marjanović told Balkan Insight he spent a decade providing party "security" that included buying votes and beating protesters. Source: [balkaninsight.com](https://balkaninsight.com/2026/10/15/rising-violence-is-a-sign-that-serbias-ruling-party-is-panicking/bi/)

### The Closer Look
**Poland looks to economic heights in a country transformed since Soviet days: The Guardian**
The Guardian closes a series on Poland today with people in Warsaw describing wages that have risen along with the cost of living. Above the city, the Varso tower, finished four years ago and the tallest building in the European Union, carries a 310-metre spire over the Palace of Culture and Science, Joseph Stalin's gift. Cezary Błaszczyk, managing director of HB Reavis in Poland, which owns the tower, said "We look down on it," and that standing taller than the palace means the country got over communism and now has a strong economy. His colleague Natalia Kasperska said a slackline walker who crossed the 500-metre gap between the buildings a few months ago made "a symbolic walk from the past to the future."

The paper sets that view against four decades since Poland left Soviet-dominated rule. Excluding oil-exporting states and financial hubs, it says incomes have converged with western levels at the fastest rate in the world, from 40 percent of the EU average in the mid-1990s to 81 percent last year. National income passed $1 trillion, or £755 billion, last year, ranking Poland among the world's 20 largest economies. International Monetary Fund projections show income per person will soon overtake Japan and Spain. Deputy foreign minister Marcin Bosacki recalled queueing after school in the 1980s for up to five hours for butter and meat while the communist government imposed martial law. The Gdańsk shipworkers' Solidarność movement and Pope John Paul II's pilgrimage in 1979 preceded democracy in 1990, Nato membership in 1999 and EU accession in 2004.

The direction of migration has turned. For years Poles left to earn more abroad, and Polish plumbers became shorthand in Britain during the fights over free movement before the Brexit vote. In each year since 2021, twice as many Polish nationals left the United Kingdom as arrived. In 2024, Germany recorded more non-Germans moving to Poland than heading the other way for the first time on record. Architects Jedrzej Kolesinski and Krzysztof Gornicki, who moved to London in their twenties and led the Foster + Partners team behind the Varso, have come back and are designing Warsaw's new airport, which the paper calls the biggest greenfield infrastructure project in Europe. Gornicki said he can do global work from Warsaw and wanted to raise a family near his parents in a city safer, greener and more affordable than London. Electric trams, cranes and dockless e-scooters fill the streets below; orders at the oldest milk bar, Prasowy, now go through a touchscreen; Parade Square, once an asphalt expanse for Soviet tanks, has been planted as Warsaw bids for the 2040 summer Olympics. The Guardian also writes that incoming capital has driven up living costs and squeezed poorer Varsovians, that income inequality is among the highest in Europe, and that political divisions are widening ahead of a general election next year. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/15/poland-economy-heights-transformed-regional-tech-hub)

### Also Today
**Ukraine war briefing: UK pledges £17m to repair Chornobyl attack damage amid fears of slipping US support: The Guardian**
Britain will provide £17 million ($23 million) to repair the Chornobyl shelter and ventilation damaged in a Russian drone attack last year, the chancellor and foreign secretary said on Thursday, citing corrosion risks. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/15/ukraine-war-briefing-uk-pledges-17m-to-repair-chornobyl-attack-damage-amid-fears-of-slipping-us-support) Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/uk-government-provide-17-million-for-chornobyl-plant-repairs-2026-10-14/)

**France 'can no longer finance' Ukraine, far-right presidential frontrunner Le Pen says: France 24**
Marine Le Pen told reporters in Brussels on Wednesday that France "can no longer finance Ukraine" because of a high deficit and weak growth, which she called an "extremely perilous situation." Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261015-france-can-no-longer-finance-ukraine-far-right-candidate-marine-le-pen-says)

**Waterford family ‘murdered by gang in arson attack over €20,000 drug debt’, son says: The Irish Times**
John James English told RTÉ the attack that killed Philip and Kim English and their sons Callum, 12, and Jayden, 8, was over a €20,000 drug debt run up by someone else, while a girl of 14 and a boy of 6 remained critically ill in Dublin. Source: [irishtimes.com](https://www.irishtimes.com/crime-law/2026/10/15/waterford-family-murdered-by-gang-in-arson-attack-over-20000-drug-debt-son-says/)

**Frontex suspends reintegration program after blowing through its budget: Politico Europe**
Frontex has suspended a reintegration program after using up its budget, ahead of a proposed expansion of the EU border agency's role in returns. Source: [politico.eu](https://www.politico.eu/article/frontex-suspends-reintegration-program-after-blowing-through-its-budget/?utm_source=RSS_Feed&utm_medium=RSS&utm_campaign=RSS_Syndication)

### Progress Watch
**Garda numbers set to reach record levels but GRA says growth ‘nowhere near enough’: The Irish Times**
The Irish Times reports that a class of about 200 recruits passing out on Friday at the Garda College in Templemore is set to push sworn Garda membership above 14,800 for the first time, from 14,683 at the end of August, a year-on-year rise of 500, past the previous record of 14,750 in March 2020. Garda headquarters says that growth has supported high-visibility policing in Dublin, Cork, Limerick and Galway, and that Commissioner Justin Kelly intends to meet a government target of 5,000 additional gardaí by 2030, about 16,500 members, broadly in line with Police Scotland. The Garda Representative Association says the pace is "nowhere near fast enough," notes that Kelly told the Public Accounts Committee the force will rely on overtime until it reaches 16,500, and says 400 members have left so far this year, against an earlier target of passing 15,000 in 2021 and 18,000 by the end of the decade. Minister for Justice Jim O'Callaghan's department says he is confident the highest-ever number of serving gardaí will be reached by the end of this year. Source: [irishtimes.com](https://www.irishtimes.com/crime-law/2026/10/15/garda-numbers-set-to-reach-record-levels-this-week-gra-says-growth-nowhere-near-enough/)

# Omni View Europe
> **Four devices of up to 27 kilograms are in a Hamburg war-crimes case over Europe's Nord Stream lines.**

**What You Need to Know:** A Hamburg court has opened proceedings over the 2022 Nord Stream blasts, with German prosecutors accusing a Ukrainian officer of helping plant devices of up to 27 kilograms on the Baltic pipelines. Elsewhere, Ukrainian authorities reported at least six people killed in overnight Russian strikes and President Volodymyr Zelensky said about 600,000 people were left without power. The Vatican said Pope Leo had successful surgery to remove a cancerous growth from his right lung.

### Lead
**Ukrainian soldier to go on trial over sabotage of Nord Stream gas pipelines: The Guardian**
A Ukrainian special forces officer, Serhii Kuznetsov, went on trial in Hamburg on Wednesday, accused by German prosecutors of taking part in the blasts that damaged the Nord Stream gas pipelines on 26 September 2022. Prosecutors accuse him of being an accomplice to war crimes by attacking civilian infrastructure, causing an explosion, damaging property and disrupting public services. He denies any involvement, and Ukraine denies involvement. He will be identified in court as Serhii K under German privacy laws, though an extradition order used his full name. Prosecutors allege he prepared and carried out the detonation of at least four incendiary devices of up to 27 kilograms at a depth of about 80 metres under the Baltic Sea, near the Danish island of Bornholm, and that six accomplices — four deep-sea divers, an explosives expert and a ship’s captain — used a rented yacht and timer-controlled explosives. The blasts burst Nord Stream 1, Russia’s main gas supply route to Germany before Moscow cut supplies in August 2022, and damaged Nord Stream 2, which Germany had suspended before Russia’s full-scale invasion and which was never put into operation. In July, German state prosecutors accused Ukrainian state authorities of ordering the attack, arguing the aim was to halt gas supplies and stop Russia using gas revenue to finance the war; President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has denied his country was involved. Kuznetsov was arrested in August 2025 on a family holiday in Italy while travelling on a false passport, and extradited to Germany last November. A further suspect, Volodymyr Zhuravlyov, was arrested in northern Croatia in August, is fighting extradition after applying for asylum there, and denies any role. The German government has declined to comment. The Alternative für Deutschland has used the case to argue that German aid for Ukraine must cease and the pipeline be reinstated. A Russian request to participate as co-plaintiffs was rejected; Gazprom, which owns Nord Stream 2, had sought that role. Kuznetsov is expected to remain silent, and his lawyers are expected to offer affidavits from two military superiors that he is prohibited from revealing his actions as a soldier. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/14/ukrainian-soldier-to-go-on-trial-over-sabotage-of-nord-stream-gas-pipelines) Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/ukrainian-ex-officer-stands-trial-germany-over-nord-stream-bombing-2026-10-14/)

### Across the Region
**Ukraine live: Russia's 'targeted' strikes on energy leave 600,000 without power, Zelensky says: France 24**
Two days after Donald Trump announced an energy ceasefire, Ukrainian authorities said heavy overnight Russian strikes killed at least six people, and President Volodymyr Zelensky said the attacks left some 600,000 people without power. Zelensky wrote that a targeted ballistic strike hit energy infrastructure covered by the ceasefire announced by the American president, and accused Russia of deliberate, ostentatious disrespect toward the United States. Russia’s defence ministry said its forces struck seven Ukrainian energy facilities and a data centre in Kyiv which it said was used to gather intelligence on Russia’s armed forces, naming heat and power plants in Kyiv and Kharkiv among the targets, and said the attack used ground-launched missiles and long-range strike drones. Kyiv’s air force said Ukraine downed four of 39 missiles. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said two people were killed and 21 injured in a missile strike on an apartment block; Zelensky said Darnytska CHP-4, which supplies heating and electricity, was hit with no early warning from partners. A technology adviser to Zelensky, Sergiy Beskrestnov, said SpaceX introduced a speed limit for Starlink terminals in motion overnight, that defence forces were not warned, and that missions were disrupted. Trump said the United States is still sharing intelligence and that Ukraine hit many sites the day before; he did not say Russia had broken a ceasefire. Russia’s foreign minister Sergey Lavrov said Ukraine does not deserve the respite a ceasefire would bring. Zelensky is due to meet Prime Minister Andy Burnham at Downing Street on Wednesday to discuss air defence supplies. Russia’s defence ministry, cited by Interfax, said it had downed 902 drones over Russian regions overnight. Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261014-live-ukraine-massive-russian-attack-on-energy-facilities-at-least-six-dead) Source: [bbc.com](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ck20r9qpw505o) Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261014-kyiv-power-plant-hit-by-russian-missile-without-warning-from-allies)

**What we know about Pope Leo XIV's lung cancer diagnosis: France 24**
The Vatican said Pope Leo underwent surgery on Tuesday to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung after a nodule was detected at a very early stage. It called the operation successful and said the pontiff would undergo additional testing. To ensure the procedure was radical, the lower lobe of the right lung was removed. A Vatican source told France 24 that further tests were being carried out to determine whether the cancer had spread. France 24 reported a 90-minute operation after which the pope woke up normally. The BBC reported the same successful removal of the lower lobe. Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261014-what-we-know-about-pope-leo-xiv-s-lung-cancer-operation) Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck1wvd9dvv22o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss) Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/pope-leo-has-cancerous-growth-removed-in-lung-operation)

**Bosnia’s New Government was Being Built as Votes Were Still Being Counted: Balkan Insight**
People in Bosnia and Herzegovina voted on 4 October, and party leaders were assembling governments before the count finished. Three days after the election, the chairmen of the Party of Democratic Action, the Party for Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the Democratic Front announced they would form the government of Sarajevo Canton. On 9 October, Dragan Covic of the Croatian Democratic Union met Nermin Niksic of the Social Democratic Party in Mostar, then met Bakir Izetbegovic of the Party of Democratic Action in Sarajevo. On Saturday Izetbegovic welcomed Semir Efendic of the Party for Bosnia and Herzegovina. On Monday Covic sat in Banja Luka with Milorad Dodik of the Alliance of Independent Social Democrats. Balkan Insight reported that Dodik is barred from holding public office because of a court conviction, and that he and Covic emerged issuing joint conditions. Professor Adnan Huskic had told BIRN before the vote that the campaign was very anaemic. Source: [balkaninsight.com](https://balkaninsight.com/2026/10/14/bosnias-new-government-was-being-built-as-votes-were-still-being-counted/bi/)

### The Closer Look
**How Europe’s most wanted cocaine trafficker turned Sierra Leone into the world’s first true narco state: The Guardian**
The price of cocaine in Europe is the stake in a Guardian investigation published on Wednesday. Intelligence assessments cited by the paper credit a 35-year-old Dutch national, Jos Leijdekkers, with importing volumes large enough to crash the European market, and say that last year he halved the drug’s wholesale price. Those sources say he is also the son-in-law of Sierra Leone’s president, Julius Maada Bio, and that he ordered the abduction of a Freetown man, Alan Jalloh. A western official told the Guardian: “It is state capture by a criminal network on a scale never seen.”

The account of that capture, as the paper’s police and intelligence sources tell it, runs from a supermarket forecourt to a boarding at sea. Witnesses described a black Toyota Rav4 forcing through rush-hour traffic outside Goodies supermarket in Freetown. Men the witnesses called burly and white pulled on balaclavas, and dragged Jalloh, 40, and two friends into the vehicle. None of the three has been seen since. Two days later, on 25 October 2025, another three men disappeared. Within a week, nine people had been seized from the city’s streets, most in daylight. Police sources were told they were dismembered and that at least one was beheaded. No bodies have been found. An officer investigating Jalloh’s abduction said: “They were exterminated to hide the truth.” Intelligence sources told the paper that at least 14 people have been killed inside Sierra Leone on Leijdekkers’ orders, and that high-ranking police are believed to have been murdered on his say-so. Officers have fled the country, those sources said.

Five months after Jalloh disappeared, the cargo ship Arconian left Freetown. By May, Spanish civil guards boarded it about 100 miles off Morocco. A guard the Guardian names as Lucas Fernández described six gunmen in the hold and, nearby, 1,279 bales of cocaine weighing between 30 and 45 tonnes, which the paper calls the largest amount of the drug ever seized. Seventeen days later, Bio addressed Oxford University. The Guardian describes him as chair of Ecowas, a region it says is home to more than 400 million people, and as someone the EU has treated as a reliable ally, with aid to Sierra Leone stretching back more than 45 years. The paper says that continued even as intelligence detailed cocaine volumes bound for Europe, and that the UN overlooked its own evidence.

The same sources warn the network is expanding. A Dutch official said the entire west Africa region is at risk. A European police source said dozens of Leijdekkers’ gunmen descended on a Dutch village last month intent on retribution, and that cocaine disputes in Europe had entered a new era. The first recorded sighting of Leijdekkers in west Africa, the investigation says, was a six-vehicle convoy in Freetown in October 2022. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/ng-interactive/2026/oct/14/europes-most-wanted-cocaine-trafficker-sierra-leone-crime-drugs-narco-state)

### Also Today
**Waterford family’s deaths in petrol bomb attack linked to local drugs gang, gardaí believe: The Irish Times**
Gardaí believe the petrol-bomb attack that killed Philip and Kim English and their children Callum, 12, and Jayden, 8, at the family home in Birchwood, Waterford, is linked to a local drugs gang, with two other people in critical condition. Source: [irishtimes.com](https://www.irishtimes.com/crime-law/2026/10/14/waterford-familys-deaths-in-petrol-bomb-attack-linked-to-local-drugs-gang-gardai-believe/)

A man has been charged with plotting an attack on the Polish prime minister, and improvised explosive devices were discovered at his home. Source: [notesfrompoland.com](https://notesfrompoland.com/2026/10/13/man-charged-with-plotting-attack-on-polish-pm/)

Euronews reported at least 11 people missing after two ships were struck off Bulgaria, and that drone strikes hit two commercial vessels off Bulgaria’s coast on Tuesday morning. Source: [euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/video/2026/10/14/latest-news-bulletin-october-14th-2026-morning) Source: [euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/14/europe-today-spanish-fm-on-euronews-black-sea-drone-attacks-eu-china-reset)

The Home Office said on Wednesday it would double the number of riot police along the French coast after the government, earlier this month, scrapped a “one in, one out” asylum deal with France that had lasted 423 days. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/14/wednesday-briefing-why-small-boat-crossings-are-here-to-stay)

### The Region and the World
**Trump says 'massive' oil, gas and mineral exploration to begin in Greenland: France 24**
President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that a massive oil, gas and mineral exploration was getting ready to begin in Greenland, without giving details of prospective American involvement. He also said Greenland is second to none for the defence of the United States and Europe, and that any future attack on the United States would have to come across the island. The United States, Denmark and Greenland last month signed a security agreement after Trump’s repeated threats to take control of the island. France 24 reported that the agreement still needs a second reading in Greenland’s parliament before a vote, and that it would expand the US military role, pave the way for two new bases and Trump’s Golden Dome missile defence system, and reaffirm Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders’ right to self-determination. Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261014-trump-says-massive-oil-gas-and-mineral-exploration-to-begin-in-greenland)

# Omni View Europe

> **Thirty-two countries warn Iran that attacks like the RAF Fairford incident will be prosecuted.**

**What You Need to Know:** Thirty-two countries warn Iran that attacks like the RAF Fairford incident will be prosecuted. Foreign ministers including those of the United Kingdom, France and Germany published a joint statement on Monday recognising the United Kingdom’s attribution of Iranian involvement in the 27 September incident at the base. The ministers said attempts to harm people on their territories through proxies would not be tolerated.

### Lead
**32 Countries Condemn Iran’s State-Backed Threats, Cite RAF Fairford Incident: Kurdistan24**
Foreign ministers from 32 countries, including the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Germany and Australia, published a joint statement on Monday condemning what they described as Iran’s use of violent attacks, covert networks and proxy actors. The ministers recognised the United Kingdom’s attribution of Iran’s involvement in an incident at RAF Fairford on 27 September, and its assessment that the event showed the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ continued willingness to act beyond Iran’s borders through covert networks and proxy actors. They listed alleged activity from lethal plotting and arson to sabotage, cyberattacks and other hybrid operations, and tied their concern to a recent campaign of attacks across Europe against Jewish communities, Iranian journalists and US interests, which the statement said was claimed by Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya, or HAYI. The statement said any attempt by Iran to threaten, silence, intimidate, harass, harm or coerce people on their territories through proxies or any other means is unacceptable, and warned that people acting for Iran or any other state would face efforts to identify, investigate, disrupt and prosecute them. The ministers pledged to hold those responsible accountable and to strengthen coordination. The Guardian reported that Andy Burnham said the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps were “almost certainly” behind threats to RAF Fairford, and described that as the firmest attribution of responsibility made so far by the UK. Source: [kurdistan24.net](https://www.kurdistan24.net/en/story/945744/32-countries-condemn-irans-state-backed-threats-cite-raf-fairford-incident)
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/13/tuesday-briefing-could-burnham-take-britain-back-towards-the-eu

### Across the Region
**What is holding back Cyprus's Schengen ambitions?: DW**
The European Commission said in July that Cyprus is technically ready to join the Schengen Area after implementing 120 recommendations from evaluations dating to 2021, covering border controls, visa policy, access to European security databases and police cooperation. On 1 October, Deputy Minister for Migration and International Protection Nicholas Ioannides said all of those recommendations are now considered implemented, and that the next step is a political agreement; with Ireland, Cyprus is one of only two EU members outside the zone. Joining still requires a unanimous decision by the EU Council after consultation with the European Parliament. According to information obtained by DW, Austria and the Netherlands have informally expressed reservations over security concerns linked to the Green Line and the British Sovereign Base Areas, without officially threatening a veto; both previously objected to Bulgaria and Romania joining. DW describes the Green Line as the roughly 180-kilometre ceasefire line dividing the Republic of Cyprus from the Turkish-controlled north since Turkey’s military intervention in 1974, not an internationally recognised state border, with the UN buffer zone monitored by UNFICYP and crossings at nine points under a special EU regulation. Source: [dw.com](https://www.dw.com/en/what-is-holding-back-cyprus-s-schengen-ambitions/a-79641488?maca=en-rss-en-eu-2092-rdf)

**Norway Details Funding Allocation for Second Andøya Launch Pad: European Spaceflight**
In its proposed state budget, published on 7 October, the Norwegian government allocated 323.3 million kroner, about 30 million euros, in 2027 toward a second orbital launch pad at Andøya Spaceport. Of that sum, 223.5 million kroner would come from the Ministry of Defence and 99.5 million kroner from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries. The project’s total budget is 646 million kroner, with the remainder expected in the 2028 budget, and Norway is targeting 2028 for completion, though parliament still has to approve the 2027 money before construction can begin. Under a revised model, the state would build and own the infrastructure, while majority state-owned Andøya Space would operate the site and lease it on terms not yet confirmed. The Norwegian Armed Forces are expected to take over security of the area around the spaceport; today Andøya Space handles safety during launches and the police handle public security. Source: [europeanspaceflight.com](https://europeanspaceflight.com/norway-details-funding-allocation-for-second-andoya-launch-pad/)

### Also Today
**Live: France braces for fresh nationwide protests over school conditions: France 24**

# Omni View Europe
> **Forty-six new projects in sixteen EU states are meant to cut reliance on any one mineral supplier.**

**What You Need to Know:** Forty-six new projects in sixteen EU states are meant to cut reliance on any one mineral supplier. The European Commission picked them from 102 applications so that, by 2030, EU capacity covers set shares of extraction, processing and recycling under the Critical Raw Materials Act. Romania accounts for two of the projects.

### Lead
**Commission selects 46 new Strategic Projects to bolster the EU’s supply of critical raw materials: The European Sting**
The European Commission said today it has selected 46 new Strategic Projects in 16 member states, chosen from 102 applications, to diversify supply and depend less on any single supplier of critical raw materials. Under the Critical Raw Materials Act, the 2030 benchmarks are that EU capacity meet at least 10 percent of annual consumption for extraction, 40 percent for processing and 25 percent for recycling. Eight projects are extraction, 11 processing and 19 recycling, plus eight integrated projects — three combining extraction and processing, five combining processing and recycling — covering 15 of 17 strategic raw materials in the Act. Battery chains are the largest cluster: seven lithium, 12 nickel, 10 cobalt, five manganese and four graphite; two magnesium and three tungsten projects are tied to defence and aerospace, and four rare-earth projects to permanent magnets. The Commission said these 46, added to 47 EU projects selected in March last year and 13 third-country projects selected in June last year, are expected to contribute to those derisking targets. Business Review reports that two of the new projects are in Romania. Source: [europeansting.com](https://europeansting.com/2026/10/12/commission-selects-46-new-strategic-projects-to-bolster-the-eus-supply-of-critical-raw-materials/) Source: [business-review.eu](https://business-review.eu/news/romania-secures-two-new-eu-strategic-raw-materials-projects-301796)

### Across the Region
**Czech Local Elections Deliver Warning to Babis’s Governing Coalition: Balkan Insight**
Czech municipal elections on October 9–10, with votes counted by Sunday midday, did not overturn the political map less than a year after Prime Minister Andrej Babis’s coalition took office, on a turnout of 48 percent. Local associations and independent candidates again took the largest share, more than 50,000 seats out of 62,000, while 22 of 27 Senate mandates in this partial election go to a second round on October 16–17. Babis said close to 1,500 council seats showed ANO is the strongest political force at all levels except the Senate; ANO finished first in six of 13 regional capitals, against eight in 2022, including Karlovy Vary, Pilsen, Ostrava and Olomouc. Balkan Insight says most analysts found ANO down on both seats and the popular vote from four years ago, with its worst-ever Prague result and a setback in Usti nad Labem, a long-time stronghold. Junior partner Motorists for Themselves broke through only in Ostrava and did poorly in Prague and Brno — leader and Foreign Minister Petr Macinka said he was not happy and not pleased — while the Freedom and Direct Democracy party of House Speaker Tomio Okamura won fewer than 170 municipal seats, and vice-chairman Radim Fiala said the party must consider what to change before the next elections. Source: [balkaninsight.com](https://balkaninsight.com/2026/10/12/czech-local-elections-deliver-warning-to-babiss-governing-coalition/rd/)

**Arla to close packaging plant in Sweden: Dairy Business Middle East & Africa**
Arla Foods said it will close the Falbygdens Ost import and packaging site in Falköping, Sweden, affecting about 60 jobs, because of long-running losses and weaker demand for much of that range. The plant imports, stores, processes and packs speciality and dessert cheeses; Arla said it does not make cheese there and does not use milk from the co-op’s farmer-owners. Dessert cheeses sold as Falbygdens will be phased out, some popular lines moving to Castello, while aged Swedish cheese stays under Kvibille. Anna Schreil, head of logistics and production in Sweden and Finland, called the decision a heavy message for staff and Falköping, and said a farmer-owned co-op has to put money where it creates the most long-term value for owners, including more Swedish milk and food security. Arla said it is in talks with the unions and will support affected workers; it will keep Osthuset on Energigatan, with about ten roles, and said that since 2023 the board has approved more than 5 billion Swedish kronor, about 446 million dollars, of investment in Sweden, including a recent 28.3 million euro expansion of the cottage-cheese plant in Falkenberg. Source: [dairybusinessmea.com](https://dairybusinessmea.com/2026/10/12/arla-to-close-packaging-plant-in-sweden/)

### Also Today
**Europe Today: Trump claims Ukraine-Russia energy ceasefire as Baltics stay on alert: Euronews**

Source: [liberties.eu](https://www.liberties.eu/en/stories/gap-analysis-2026/45807)

### The Region and the World
**Can China and the EU avert a trade war?: ThinkChina**
Europe’s goods deficit with China reached 359.3 billion euros last year, more than double the 2019 gap, and Brussels says it cannot accept a deficit now running at 1.1 billion euros a day, which it attributes to unfair Chinese trade practices. Beijing says those figures do not hold up: nearly half of China-EU trade is intermediate goods that European firms buy, upgrade and sell on, so the surplus sits in China while Europe takes the profit, and the EU keeps a long-running services surplus with China. Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic held two days of talks in Beijing with Commerce Minister Wang Wentao from October 8, ahead of an EU summit in Brussels this week on the response to Chinese competition. Talks ended late Friday, October 9, with a 16-point consensus covering trade and investment, export controls and intellectual property; China agreed to curb hybrid-vehicle exports to the bloc, a step aimed at avoiding harsher restrictions. ThinkChina says that gesture is unlikely to reshape the wider relationship soon, and that it buys time for further talks in January and March. Source: [thinkchina.sg](https://www.thinkchina.sg/economy/can-china-and-eu-avert-trade-war)

### Both Sides: Retiring France’s central-bank-held debt
France’s argument is over a slice of public debt the state already holds on its own books, not over a bill with a named vote date. Emmanuel Moulin, governor of France’s central bank, wants large budget cuts. His stated reason is the risk of being gradually strangled by rising interest rates. Jean-Luc Mélenchon, leader of La France Insoumise and a presidential contender, has instead proposed dealing with about 600 billion euros — 673 billion dollars, or 18 percent of France’s aggregate public debt. Those are French government bonds the central bank owns and will hold to maturity. At maturity, the essay says, taxpayers would pay more tax, or borrow again, to repay their own central bank. Mélenchon’s case is that it is absurd for one arm of the French state to borrow 600 billion euros in order to pay another arm. His alternative is a swap between the Treasury and the central bank that, in practice, retires that debt and frees room for investment. The essay says the plan draws on debt-swap proposals made in 2015 by a then Greek finance minister. Moulin’s camp treats spending cuts as the way to keep interest costs from closing in. Mélenchon’s camp treats the internal debt as a loop that cuts would not break, and as space that could fund investment instead. Source: [businessamlive.com](https://businessamlive.com/melenchon-is-right-about-frances-debt/)

> **Nearly two thousand files put Germany's ex-spy chief in pretrial detention.**

**What You Need to Know:** Nearly two thousand files have put Germany's former foreign-intelligence chief in pretrial detention, on charges he has denied through his lawyers. Italy has raised its deficit targets after new defense and energy borrowing, and UK drivers can now see station fuel prices inside Google Maps and Waze.

### Lead
**‘Stab to the heart’: arrest of German ex-spymaster sparks calls for reform: The Guardian**
Federal prosecutors have charged August Hanning, who led Germany's federal foreign intelligence service, the BND, from 1998 to 2005, with treasonous espionage and with handing state secrets to a foreign power. They believe he paid his former chief of staff, identified only as Manfred D, to remove nearly 2,000 documents, at least some classified, over 12 years, and then used that intelligence for clients of a private consulting firm he started after retirement. On Tuesday, masked commandos led the 80-year-old from his estate in Nordwalde to a police van without handcuffs; experts told The Guardian the detention of someone of his former rank is a first in a western democracy. Konstantin von Notz, a Bundestag member on the parliamentary intelligence supervisory committee, said the case could become a national scandal and warned of a devastating loss of trust among partner countries. Hanning is in pretrial detention; his lawyers deny he passed confidential documents to foreign powers, and a conviction could mean 10 years in prison. Many of the files are believed to have been briefing papers for top officials, including the chancellor. Hanning once called Germany's own services "vegetarians" among carnivores and demanded broader powers. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/11/stab-to-the-heart-arrest-of-german-ex-spymaster-sparks-calls-for-reform)

### Across the Region
**After France, is Italy next? Goldman Sachs flags bond risks as Rome's deficit widens: CNBC**
Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government on October 2 approved an extra 28 billion euros in borrowing over two years, split evenly between defense and energy, and will present the budget next week. The 2027 deficit target is now 3.4 percent of GDP and the 2028 target 3.2 percent, up from April projections of 2.8 percent and 2.5 percent; each area is about 0.3 percent of GDP a year in those two years. Filippo Taddei, senior European economist at Goldman Sachs, said wider deficits and higher yields could push Italy's debt ratio to Europe's highest by 2028 and lift fiscal risk premia before a general election due no later than December 22, 2027. On Friday, CNBC put France's 10-year yield at 4.85 percent and Italy's at 4.55 percent, with the gap to German Bunds about 108 basis points. PIMCO said domestic ownership and stronger fundamentals offer support for Italian bonds. Source: [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/11/italy-government-bonds-sovereign-debt-giorgia-meloni.html)

Sarah-Jayne Williams, Global Product Partnerships Director at Google Maps and Waze, said a search for petrol or fuel returns the latest prices, rates appear on the map, and a station listing shows every fuel it sells. ### Both Sides: Italy's wider deficit for defense and energy
Italy's government is changing its budget path, and markets are arguing over whether that path is manageable. On October 2, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's center-right government approved an extra 28 billion euros in borrowing over two years for defense and energy. The cabinet will present the budget next week. The new targets put the 2027 deficit at 3.4 percent of GDP and the 2028 deficit at 3.2 percent, up from April projections of 2.8 percent and 2.5 percent.

The case for going ahead is the government's own allocation. The money is split evenly between defense and energy, each worth about 0.3 percent of GDP a year in 2027 and 2028. CNBC reports the plans were scaled back, yet they remain the spending Meloni's cabinet chose to finance by borrowing, in a week when French debt strains have already drawn investors toward eurozone public finances. PIMCO's stated reason for staying with Italian bonds is domestic ownership and stronger fundamentals, which it says offer support even if an election adds uncertainty.

The case against a calm reading comes from Filippo Taddei, senior European economist at Goldman Sachs. He says wider deficits and higher yields could push Italy's debt ratio to Europe's highest by 2028, and that fiscal risk premia could rise before a general election due no later than December 22, 2027. On Friday, CNBC recorded France's 10-year yield at 4.85 percent and Italy's at 4.55 percent, with the spread to German Bunds about 108 basis points. Taddei's point is that the new targets sit above earlier projections and above Goldman's forecasts, so the bond market may charge Italy more, not less, as the vote approaches.

Both sides are working from the same approved sum and the same new deficit targets. The next dated step in the reporting is next week's budget presentation; the election deadline Goldman cites is December 22, 2027.

# Omni View Europe
> **Three hundred thousand tons of Russian diesel are cleared for sale, testing Europe's sanctions on Moscow.**

**What You Need to Know:** Three hundred thousand tons of Russian diesel are cleared for sale, testing Europe's sanctions on Moscow. After a Friday call with Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump said Russia would also send 500,000 tons in November and 1,000,000 tons after that, and the US Treasury moved to license the supply. Volodymyr Zelensky and the UK government rejected any easing of pressure on Moscow, while London said it still backs US-led peace efforts.

### Lead
**Ukraine War, Day 1,689: Trump — Putin Is Selling Diesel Fuel to US: EA WorldView**
A day after US envoys briefed Donald Trump on Ukraine proposals, Trump said a Friday call with Vladimir Putin agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 tons of diesel to the American and global marketplace, another 500,000 tons in November, and 1,000,000 tons immediately thereafter. EA WorldView reports the US Treasury said the Office of Foreign Assets Control is immediately issuing a temporary general license for Russian diesel on the global market, and that US diesel reached a record $6.52 a gallon last month, more than double a year earlier. Volodymyr Zelensky said the decision is not honest, is unworthy of partners, and is a weak decision, and that it looks like a birthday present for Putin, who turned 74 this week. The UK government said it will keep military and financial support for Ukraine and the toughest sanctions regime it has imposed, that Russia has rejected ceasefires while attacking civilians and energy, and that it still fully supports US-led efforts for a just and lasting peace while watching energy prices. Steve Witkoff said Friday's Miami meeting with the E3 — Britain, France and Germany — the European Commission, Ukraine and NATO held constructive talks on ending the war ahead of winter; Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned a stalemate can end in escalation that reaches neighbouring NATO states. Al Jazeera reported US lawmakers, Zelensky and European allies criticised the diesel deal, and that hours later a Ukrainian drone hit a Russian fuel site; EA WorldView reported a fire at the Yug Rusi oil-loading terminal in Rostov-on-Don and four civilians killed and four injured in a Saturday strike on a residential building in Zaporizhzhia. Source: [eaworldview.com](https://eaworldview.com/2026/10/ukraine-war-trump-putin-diesel/)

### Across the Region
**As Russia escalates, EU realises its Ukraine support won't be enough: Euronews**
European diplomats say Russia's escalation is exposing the limits of the European Union's multibillion-euro support for Ukraine. One diplomat, speaking anonymously, said the war will last longer than thought and that further needs are not yet matched by a plan; another said the EU must double down on support for Ukraine and pressure on Russia. Euronews reports the €90 billion loan leaders agreed last year, meant to cover two-thirds of Ukraine's needs for 2026 and 2027, was designed on the premise the war would end sometime this year. Railways, bridges, cargo vessels, power stations, data centres, warehouses, medical centres, schools and kindergartens have been hit in recent days, a Black Sea blockade is blocking grain sales, and on Thursday Russia plunged Kyiv into darkness. Volodymyr Zelensky called the strikes terror against people and life; European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called them war crimes. Source: [euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/10/as-russia-escalates-its-war-the-eu-admits-its-support-for-ukraine-wont-be-enough)

**Scotland to develop 'War Book' with UK as military chiefs warn of conflict by 2030: The Herald**
Scotland is to draft a new War Book with the UK as military leaders warn of a growing threat of large-scale conflict by 2030. The Herald reports the format, first developed early last century and used in the Cold War for a nuclear attack, was shelved after that threat faded and is being revived because of an increased threat to Nato from Russia. It is separate from armed-forces plans and is meant as a whole-of-society home-defence document; defence stays reserved to Westminster, but ministers recognise devolved health, transport and infrastructure would be hit in a war. A senior Scottish Government civil servant said on Thursday in Edinburgh that Scotland will work with the UK Government to influence the book, led by the Cabinet Office, and that this is the first time the Scottish Government has been involved in drafting it. Source: [heraldscotland.com](https://www.heraldscotland.com/news/26623873.scotland-develop-war-book-uk-amid-growing-threats/)

### Also Today
**European Commission has raised concerns with Ukraine regarding continued funding of telethon: Censor**

Source: [irishtimes.com](https://www.irishtimes.com/crime-law/courts/2026/10/10/school-shootings-transgender-rights-among-reasons-for-us-citizens-seeking-asylum-in-ireland/)

### The Region and the World
**A shameful and unfortunate decision — Trump criticized Norway over the Nobel Peace Prize: UNN**
Donald Trump aimed his Nobel complaint at Norway, where the Nobel Committee sits, hours after this year's Peace Prize went to Navanethem Pillay of South Africa. UNN, citing Reuters, reports he called the decision shameful and regrettable and an indelible stain on Norway, and at a rally in Syracuse, New York, called Pillay a mysterious person and said he had never heard of her. Pillay is a former judge at the International Criminal Court who led a UN report concluding that Israel committed genocide in Gaza. He told Norway: we will not forget this. Source: [unn.ua](https://unn.ua/en/news/a-shameful-and-unfortunate-decision-trump-criticized-norway-over-the-nobel-peace-prize)

### Both Sides: A US license for Russian diesel
The decision in front of Europe is whether a US license letting Russian diesel onto world markets is an energy fix partners should live with, or a crack in the sanctions wall around Moscow's war.

Donald Trump's case, in his own post after Friday's call with Vladimir Putin, is price. He said Russia will supply diesel immediately and in November, and that prices for Americans, farmers, ranchers and truckers will come down fast. EA WorldView reports US diesel hit a record $6.52 a gallon last month, more than double a year ago, and that Trump tied the spike to his war on Iran and control of the Strait of Hormuz ahead of November's midterm elections. The US Treasury said it is issuing a temporary general license so that supply can reach the global market. The UK government recognises that conflicts can move energy prices and the cost of living, and says it fully supports US-led efforts toward a just and lasting peace.

The case against comes from Kyiv and from London's sanctions line. Volodymyr Zelensky said the agreement is not honest, is unworthy of partners, and is a weak decision, and that it looks like a birthday present for Putin. Al Jazeera reports he called it a gift to Putin, and that US lawmakers and European allies criticised the deal. The UK government said it will maintain the toughest sanctions regime it has ever imposed, raise the cost of Putin's aggression, and keep military and financial support so Ukraine can defend itself. It said Ukraine has shown it is serious about peace, Russia has rejected full and partial ceasefires while striking civilians and energy, and Russia could end the war today.

Both sides are acting on the same link between the war and fuel: Trump is moving supply because diesel is expensive, and the UK says it is monitoring energy markets even as it refuses to loosen its own sanctions. Next, on the record, is immediate licensed supply, a further 500,000 tons in November, and 1,000,000 tons after that. Britain says it remains in close contact with the US, Ukraine and other allies.

> **A nearly forty-fold cut hits Russia’s cancer patients in twenty twenty-seven as defence takes thirty-five percent.**

**What You Need to Know:** Russia’s federal cancer programme is set to shrink from 44.9 billion roubles to 3.87 billion in 2027, Euronews reports, while defence reaches 35 percent of federal spending, the highest share since the Soviet collapse. In Madrid, tens of thousands marched after the death of evicted pensioner Maricarmen Abascal. The European Commission fined Kingspan 40 million euros for misleading information in a merger review it later abandoned.

### Lead
**Russia slashes cancer care as defence spending hits post-Soviet record: Euronews**
Euronews reports that Russia’s federal cancer programme budget falls from 44.9 billion roubles to 3.87 billion roubles in 2027, a nearly forty-fold reduction against 2025 levels. Defence spending reaches 35 percent of all federal expenditure, the highest share since the Soviet Union collapsed. The cut is the budget figure Euronews publishes for the cancer programme, not a claim that treatment has already stopped. Patients who depend on that federal programme are the people the smaller 2027 line reaches. The same account ties the reduction to defence taking that record share of the federal budget. Source: [euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/09/russia-slashes-cancer-care-as-defence-spending-hits-post-soviet-record)

### Across the Region
**Tens of thousands march in Madrid to mourn pensioner whose eviction sparked housing protests: France 24**
Tens of thousands marched in Madrid on Thursday after 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal died on Wednesday, two weeks after eviction from the flat she had lived in for 70 years, the September removal that had already fed housing protests and a call for early elections. A provisional estimate by the central government’s delegation in the Madrid region put the crowd at 20,000. Abascal, who used a wheelchair, died in hospital after the company that owned the flat raised the rent sharply, and mourners walked from Puerta del Sol, where hundreds are camping, about three kilometres to her former home in Retiro. Teacher Rosa Marin told AFP that Abascal “will be an icon of struggle,” and marchers chanted “they aren’t deaths, they are murders.” Photography teacher Anton Alexander told AFP the protests have put housing at the heart of the 29 November election. Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261009-tens-of-thousands-march-in-madrid-to-mourn-pensioner-whose-eviction-sparked-housing-protests)

**Commission fines Kingspan €40 million for providing incorrect and misleading information during merger investigation: The European Sting**
The European Commission has fined Kingspan 40 million euros for incorrect and misleading information during its 2021 review of Kingspan’s planned acquisition of Trimo, a deal Kingspan later abandoned. Both firms make mineral fibre sandwich panels for industrial and commercial buildings. The Commission opened the information investigation in November 2022 and, on 19 March 2024, sent a statement of objections alleging six infringements, then dropped two. It now finds four infringements, committed at least negligently, including misleading information on how Kingspan tracks penetration rates for those panels, incorrect or misleading information on bidding data, and incorrect information on board members’ involvement in the Trimo plan, other acquisitions, industry trends and strategy. Source: [europeansting.com](https://europeansting.com/2026/10/09/commission-fines-kingspan-e40-million-for-providing-incorrect-and-misleading-information-during-merger-investigation/)

China has rejected a European Union request to restrict hybrid-car exports to Europe during talks in Beijing by Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič, EU Today reports, and the Commission is considering safeguard limits or extra tariffs once shipments pass thresholds still under discussion. EU countervailing duties imposed in October 2024 covered Chinese battery-electric vehicles and not hybrids, after which Chinese makers expanded in Europe’s hybrid market. ### Both Sides: Abortion-pill deceit after UK decriminalisation
What is being stated is how far last year’s parliamentary amendment goes. MPs voted through a change that decriminalises abortion up to birth for any woman acting in relation to her own pregnancy, including sex selection, and this week the government published an Equalities Impact Assessment on removing women from that criminal law. The assessment, as quoted by Pregnancy Help News from Christian Concern, says it would never be a criminal offence for a pregnant woman to terminate her pregnancy at any gestation, including beyond 24 weeks. It also says it would not be a criminal offence for a woman to deceive a registered medical practitioner about gestation in order to obtain abortion pills by post beyond the 10-week limit.

The government’s case, in that assessment, is that once a woman is outside the criminal offence for ending her own pregnancy, deceiving a doctor to get those pills is not itself a crime for her. The case against treating deception as lawful comes from Christian Concern and health expert Kevin Duffy, who say the 10-week limit exists because the pills are not approved beyond it and carry serious safety risks. The same article says the World Health Organisation recommends that medical abortion at 12 weeks or more be managed by doctors in a healthcare setting, that the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists endorses that position, and that BPAS, MSI-RC and NUPAS no longer provide medical abortion in clinic beyond 10 weeks. Christian Concern adds that decriminalising abortion does not necessarily mean deception stops being an offence, and that phone-based supply cannot check coercion or gestation.

Both the assessment and its critics are talking about the same voted amendment and the same 10-week pills-by-post limit, which the article calls widely accepted. The latest step in the record is this week’s publication of the assessment. Source: [pregnancyhelpnews.com](https://pregnancyhelpnews.com/uk-government-claims-abortion-pill-deceit-is-not-a-crime)

> **Nearly 200 years on, Britain keeps its Jerusalem building open under a new name after Israel moved to shut it.**

**What You Need to Know:** Britain says its Jerusalem consulate building stays open from today as the UK Mission, Jerusalem, after talks with Israel, which Sky News reported had confirmed a closure. The UK government says it does not accept that Israel has the legal right to close that mission, has withdrawn some staff and families, and will not take reciprocal action while talks continue. Danish intelligence says sabotage against defense suppliers has moved from planning into operations, and students in France are back in the streets.

### Lead
**Foreign Secretary statement on the UK's diplomatic presence in Jerusalem: GOV.UK**
A Foreign Secretary statement said that, after discussions with the Government of Israel, the Consulate General building will not close and will be known from today as the UK Mission, Jerusalem. The UK government said it does not accept that Israel has the legal right to close the British Consulate General, there for nearly 200 years, and it restated its long-standing view that East Jerusalem is occupied territory. It said the UK Mission, Jerusalem is independent and operational and will keep delivering services and work with the Palestinian people, so Britain maintains its presence and its role in support of a two-state solution. Without an understanding, the statement said, Britain would not have the assurances it needs for staff and premises, so it has temporarily withdrawn a number of staff and families and will work in the coming months to build that presence back up. The UK said it will not take reciprocal action while those discussions are underway and credible, and that it stands by measures taken on 8 September with international partners in support of a two-state solution. Sky News reported that Israel has confirmed it is closing the British consulate in East Jerusalem after a UK ban on trade with West Bank settlements, which Sky described as illegal. Source: [gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/foreign-secretary-statement-on-the-uks-diplomatic-presence-in-jerusalem)
https://news.sky.com/story/israel-confirms-it-is-closing-the-british-consulate-in-east-jerusalem-after-uk-ban-on-trade-with-illegal-west-bank-settlements-13596361

**Russia Steps Up Sabotage Attacks on Danish Defense Firms, Intelligence Says: Kyiv Post**

She told a homeland security conference that spring saw a lot of planning and very little carried out, while early summer saw many more operations actually run, in remarks Kyiv Post attributed to Reuters. Christensen said Moscow is now trying to hit weapons production because earlier broad targeting did not deter NATO from supporting Ukraine, and she described the shift as a significant escalation in hybrid warfare. She cited an April list from Russia's Defense Ministry naming European drone and drone-component manufacturers as potential military targets, and PET says Russia is using untrained proxies recruited through Telegram, including homeless people and people addicted to drugs, moving from reconnaissance to sabotage. The Russian Embassy in Copenhagen rejected the allegations Wednesday as unfounded claims, and Russia has repeatedly denied involvement in sabotage or hybrid warfare. ### Both Sides: Genetically modified crop imports
The European Commission has approved or renewed authorizations for seven genetically modified crops, and the question is whether those import approvals should stand when governments in the member states would not vote them through.

The case for the decisions is the one the Commission acted on: favorable assessments by the European Food Safety Authority. UkrAgroConsult reports that the Commission approved or renewed seven events in June and September 2026 — four soybean events and three corn events — for food and animal feed. The expansion is particularly important, that report says, for the European feed sector, which relies heavily on imported soybeans and corn. The new and renewed approvals broaden the shipments that can enter the EU market for processing and use in animal feed. The list is soybean MON 94637, GMB151 crossed with DAS-44406-6, and MON 94313; corn DP202216 crossed with NK603 and DAS-40278-9; and renewals for corn NK603 crossed with T25, corn MON 87460, and soybean MON 87705. The Commission adopted the decisions after member states failed to reach a qualified majority either for or against.

The case against is the one member states put on the record in those votes: public opposition to genetically modified crops, the precautionary principle, scientific concerns, and political considerations. They did not gather a qualified majority to stop the authorizations. They also did not gather one to pass them.

What both the approvals and the objections leave in place is the scope of the decisions themselves: imports and processing only, with no authorization to grow the crops in the EU, a term of 10 years, and a requirement that products comply with EU labeling and traceability rules. Those authorizations now run for that 10-year term. Source: [ukragroconsult.com](https://ukragroconsult.com/en/news/european-commission-authorizes-imports-of-seven-new-gm-soybean-and-corn-events/)

> **Finland orders a halt at two Google sites until environmental reviews finish.**

**What You Need to Know:** Finland has ordered a halt to preparatory work at two Google data-centre sites until environmental reviews are finished, after an agency found forest already cleared. Norway’s minority government wants to draw about 63.6 billion dollars from its sovereign wealth fund in 2027. Ukrainian officials say a Russian missile attack on Kyiv overnight killed two people.

### Lead
**Finland orders halt to work on Google data centre sites: Al Jazeera**
Finland’s Supervisory Agency, the LVV, has ordered Tuike Finland, the company representing Google, to suspend by 23 October 2026 all preparatory work that would significantly alter the environment at planned data-centre sites in Muhos and Kajaani, until compulsory environmental impact assessments are completed. Google said in September it would invest 13 billion euros, about 14.6 billion dollars, in Finnish digital infrastructure over two years, and called the projects in Muhos, Vaala, Kajaani and Hamina its single biggest investment in Europe. The LVV is investigating whether hundreds of hectares of forest were cleared without a mandatory assessment; environment-department head Tommi Muilu said trees have been removed, topsoil stripped, site roads and storage areas built, and ditches altered. Hanna Halmeenpaa, chair of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation, told AFP that nature sites which should be preserved had been logged across a deforested area of more than 300 hectares. Tuike Finland must explain how it intends to proceed by 14 October, and the LVV said it could face enforcement proceedings if it does not comply. Google spokesman Sondre Ronander told AFP the company acknowledged shortcomings, would study the findings and follow the guidance, and said landscaping plans include planting trees across 130 hectares at Muhos; opposition parties last month called for a national permit system to prevent power shortages and soaring energy prices. Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/7/finland-orders-halt-to-work-on-google-data-sites-over-environment-concerns)

The government said the proposal is estimated to have a neutral effect on economic activity next year. It put the structural non-oil deficit for 2027 at 2.7 percent of the fund’s projected value at the end of 2026, in line with the current year. Mainland GDP is now expected to grow 1.1 percent this year, against 1.7 percent seen in May, and 1.7 percent in 2027, up from 1.6 percent previously; core inflation is seen at 3.1 percent in 2026, down from 3.2 percent in May, and at 2.8 percent in 2027, against 2.6 percent seen previously. Source: [english.aawsat.com](https://english.aawsat.com/business/5326874-norway-plans-spend-636-billion-wealth-fund-2027) https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-07/norway-seeks-to-keep-wealth-fund-spending-steady-in-2027-budget

The European Commission on Tuesday proposed up to 15 years of post-accession safeguards that could punish new member states for bad behaviour, in a pre-enlargement policy review the European Council had asked for in June 2024 and had wanted ready by spring 2025. The review was delayed several times because of political sensitivities in EU capitals. It is aimed at membership frontrunners Montenegro, Albania, Moldova and Ukraine, each of which is to receive an accession roadmap this month. Commission president Ursula von der Leyen has called enlargement a geopolitical imperative; the Commission suggests new members promise, for an unspecified time, not to oppose EU decisions on future enlargements because of bilateral disputes, while enlargement commissioner Marta Kos said that commitment would be voluntary. On the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks — which Euronews said killed around 1,200 people in Israel, with 251 taken hostage, and were followed by an Israeli offensive in Gaza that has killed over 70,000 Palestinians — the European Parliament became the scene of a clash over an Israeli flag. Euronews reported that on Monday evening Rima Hassan, a France Unbowed MEP, knocked over an Israeli flag at an exhibition for victims of the attack; photos on social media showed the Israeli and EU flags on the floor. Hassan acknowledged removing the Israeli flag, denied intentionally toppling the EU flag, and her office said neither flag was stepped on or damaged; she framed the act as a response to Israeli state support for the exhibition and claimed speeches there denied the existence of Palestine. Centre-right MEP François-Xavier Bellamy called the act a form of complicity with those who want to reintroduce antisemitic hatred in Europe, and Israeli foreign minister Gideon Sa’ar called the scenes shameful, outrageous, but sadly not surprising. ### Both Sides: Age bans or school lessons for young consumers online?
The question is whether the European Union should rely on age limits to protect minors online, or whether schools must teach consumer rights as well. The strongest case for limits is the one set out in the Commission President’s State of the Union address on 16 September 2026: upcoming EU KIDS legislation would put the protection of young people in the digital environment at the core of the Union’s agenda, and would include strict rules such as a ban on social media before the age of 13. The strongest case for classrooms comes from Tiziana Toto, head of national consumer policies at Cittadinanzattiva APS, and Cinzia Pollio, a senior project manager there. They argue that without education on awareness and the responsible use of new technologies, an approach built only on limits and restrictions postpones the problem rather than solving it, and that consumer literacy should be an integral part of school curricula across Europe. Cittadinanzattiva is making that case with consumer associations EEKE in Greece and InfoCons in Romania, with support from iliad and co-funding from the European Union’s Single Market Programme, through the CoRe Consumer Regeneration project. Italian MEP Denis Nesci of the ECR Group is hosting the project’s closing event on 14 October 2026, from 11:00 to 13:00 Central European Summer Time, in Room 1H1 of the European Parliament in Brussels and online. The fact both sides share is that minors face real risks online and that those risks now belong on the Union’s political agenda. The next step dated in the reporting is that 14 October meeting, which the organisers describe as the place for lessons from 16 schools and hundreds of students and for policy recommendations. Source: [innovationnewsnetwork.com](https://www.innovationnewsnetwork.com/consumer-rights-education-takes-centre-stage-at-eu-parliament/74499/)

# Omni View Europe
> **Six hundred fifty drones aimed at Moscow kill one man, Russian officials say.**

**What You Need to Know:** Russian officials say an overnight wave of 650 drones toward Moscow killed one man, in one of the largest such attacks on the capital in two years. The European Commission has ruled that Poland cannot pay about €26 million to expand a MAN Trucks plant. Britain’s government has accepted all 44 recommendations on regulating artificial intelligence in healthcare.

### Lead
**Ukraine hits Moscow with one of its largest drone attacks in two years: France 24**
France 24 reports that Ukraine launched an overnight drone attack on Moscow that Russian authorities, speaking on Tuesday, called one of the largest on the capital in two years. The Russian state agency TASS said the strike was the second-largest drone attack on Moscow and the surrounding region in that period. Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said Russia downed most of the 650 drones sent toward the capital, including 105 downed close to the city. Regional governor Andrei Vorobyov said a 20-year-old man was killed in a village on the outskirts and that several homes were damaged. The Ria Novosti agency reported that the strikes wounded six people. France 24 notes that both Ukraine and Russia have stepped up long-range strikes on civilian and industrial targets, including energy, transport, ports and ships in the Black Sea, and that Russia has said it plans to increase infrastructure strikes, including in Kyiv, as winter approaches. Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261006-massive-ukrainian-drone-attack-targets-moscow-russian-officials-say)

### Across the Region
**Commission finds Polish support for MAN Trucks factory expansion incompatible State aid: The European Sting**
The European Commission has concluded that Poland’s plan to support extra capacity at a MAN Trucks factory in Niepołomice, in the Małopolskie region, breaks EU state-aid rules, so Poland cannot pay the money. The aid, about €26 million, or PLN 116 million, was opened to an in-depth investigation in July 2025. The Commission’s early view was that the project would help jobs in a less advantaged region, but it doubted the plan met the Guidelines on Regional State Aid. After the full inquiry, the Commission said Poland had not proved the aid decided MAN Trucks’ choice of Poland, and the evidence did not show the company would have built elsewhere without it. The Commission also said Poland had not shown the sum was the minimum needed, so the support had no real incentive effect and was not proportionate. Source: [europeansting.com](https://europeansting.com/2026/10/06/commission-finds-polish-support-for-man-trucks-factory-expansion-incompatible-state-aid/)

**Government backs recommendations of NHS doctors-led AI Commission: GOV.UK**
On 6 October 2026 the UK government said it will accept all 44 recommendations of the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare, published on 10 September, and set out how they will be delivered across the UK. The Commission found that rules must move to a more proportionate, lifecycle-based system, with AI medical devices watched through their working life rather than judged once. ### Both Sides: Limits on new EU members
What is being decided is how the European Union would stay workable if Ukraine and other candidates join. The European Commission is set to unveil proposals on Tuesday, Kyiv Post reports, after months of delay while governments pushed different ideas.

The case for safeguards starts with money, votes and past blockages. Diplomats expect steps to stop new members disrupting decisions or drawing too many resources, including a promise not to use the veto in key areas and limits on Common Agricultural Policy subsidies. Enlargement commissioner Marta Kos said in August, “We must make sure we do not let in Trojan horses,” and that such measures are “a must-have, not a nice-to-have,” so the Union can accept new members with confidence. The fear stated in the reporting is that new members, especially Ukraine, could strain the budget and make decisions unmanageable, with Hungary’s repeated blockages under Viktor Orban treated as the lesson.

The case against a lesser status starts with the risk of a permanent waiting room. Chancellor Friedrich Merz earlier this year floated associate membership, under which countries could attend EU meetings but not vote. That plan received short shrift from a raft of EU countries and from Ukraine, who saw it as a way of trapping applicants in a halfway house. There has also been pushback against speeding the process up.

The shared ground is the queue. Russia’s 2022 invasion gave fresh impetus to enlargement. Ukraine and Moldova are among four frontrunners, Montenegro is pressing to become the 28th member next year, and Albania is not far behind. Brussels insists enlargement is crucial for the EU’s future. The next step is the Commission proposal Kyiv Post says is due Tuesday. Source: [kyivpost.com](https://www.kyivpost.com/post/86205)

**What You Need to Know:** More than three thousand migrants left a Ceuta beach camp for police processing. Officers began clearing Trampolín Beach on Sunday and are busing people to a temporary reception centre. Britain’s Greens voted to call Zionism racism, and a Russian draft budget puts a record share into the military.

### Lead
**Spanish police remove over 3,000 migrants from Ceuta beach camp: Euronews**
Spanish police began dismantling a migrant settlement on Trampolín Beach in Ceuta on Sunday, escorting people onto buses while officers in riot gear moved through the crowded site. Euronews reported that more than 3,000 migrants had reportedly been living there for weeks in hundreds of tents, often sleeping on cardboard sheets. The operation brings in the National Police, the Civil Guard, local police and the Ceuta General Command. People taken off the beach are going by bus to the CATE temporary reception centre for initial police processing, so the camp is being replaced by formal processing rather than left in place. ### Across the Region
**UK Green Party votes to define Zionism as racism: The Business Standard**
Britain’s Green Party voted at its annual conference to define Zionism as a form of racism and an “ethnonationalist political project.” The motion passed by 1,022 votes to 813. It calls on the UK government to end all arms trade with Israel, backs the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions movement and a full arms embargo, and supports a single democratic state throughout historic Palestine plus the Palestinian right of return. Leader Zack Polanski, who did not vote, and other members then pledged to oppose “genocide, ethnic cleansing, apartheid and the illegal occupation” and criticised the Netanyahu government; co-deputy leader Mothin Ali tied the vote to the casualty toll of Israel’s war on Gaza. Israel’s Foreign Ministry said the policy went “far beyond the boundaries of legitimate political debate,” accused the party of adopting “the elimination of the State of Israel through armed struggle,” and said it now considers the Greens as legitimising terrorism; President Isaac Herzog called the motion “a disgrace and a shame,” and the UK’s Movement for Progressive Judaism said the party had “made antisemitism party policy.” Source: [tbsnews.net](https://www.tbsnews.net/worldbiz/europe/uk-green-party-votes-define-zionism-racism-1563041)
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/4/israel-lashes-out-as-uks-green-party-formally-defines-zionism-as-racism

**Russia's invasion of Ukraine on track to be one of the most expensive wars of the century: The New Voice of Ukraine**
The Moscow Times, as reported by The New Voice of Ukraine, says the Kremlin has earmarked a record 35 percent of its 2027 budget for the military, a proposed 17.1 trillion rubles, or 203 billion dollars. Janis Kluge of the German Institute for International and Security Affairs estimates Russia has spent 58.3 trillion rubles, about 692 billion dollars, on the military and weapons procurement over the first five years of the war. The draft projects accumulated military spending of 907 billion dollars by 2028, above the central bank’s 743 billion dollars in gold and foreign-currency reserves, and earmarks 50 trillion rubles, 593 billion dollars, for defense over three years.
